extracted.intended_audience: general readers (Wikipedia audience); researchers or members of the public seeking an overview of TikTok's features, history, policies, and controversies
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive Wikipedia article summarizing TikTok (and Douyin): its history, corporate structure, features, moderation policies, controversies, viral trends, and regulatory developments. The page is descriptive rather than prescriptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video duration limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Hosts user-submitted videos, which range in duration from three seconds to 60 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the supported video length range that creators can use; relevant when producing content to fit platform constraints and user expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic recommendation behavior ('For You' page)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'For You' page is an endless feed of videos recommended to users based on their activity; TikTok's algorithm monitors a wider array of behaviors during video viewing (beyond likes, clicks, or follows) to refine recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how content is distributed and why certain videos go viral — content creators should optimize for watch behaviour signals and engagement rather than just likes/follows. The article notes the algorithm can make the app 'hard to disengage from' and contrasts TikTok's approach with other networks that base recommendations on social relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account privacy default and settings
rubrics_metrics.description: The mobile app allows users to set their accounts as 'private'. When first downloading the app, the user's account is public by default. The user can change to private. Private content remains visible to TikTok but is blocked from TikTok users who the account holder has not authorized to view their content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes default privacy posture and how users can restrict visibility; important for creators and parents to understand discoverability and exposure risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction controls (comments/messages/reacts/duets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Users can choose whether any other user, or only their 'friends', may interact with them through the app via comments, messages, or 'react' or 'duet' videos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies granular controls for who may interact with a user's content; creators should set interaction privacy consistent with intended audience. The 'react' feature places a creator's reaction in a movable small window; duet use can be restricted by privacy settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duet/stitch permission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'duet' feature is only able to be used if both parties adjust the privacy settings. Users can also use portions of other TikTok videos by creating a 'stitch'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that reuse/collaboration features depend on participant privacy choices; creators concerned about reuse should configure settings accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live feature eligibility and monetization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'live' feature is available only to those who have at least 1,000 followers and are over 16 years old. If over 18, the user's followers can send virtual 'gifts' that can later be exchanged for money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets minimum follower and age thresholds to access live-streaming and gift monetization; relevant for creators planning to monetize via live content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tip button eligibility and terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts of users that are of age, have at least 100,000 followers and agree to the terms can activate a 'Tip' button on their profile, which allows followers to tip any amount, starting from $1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines conditions for enabling direct tipping as a monetization channel; creators seeking tips must meet follower and age requirements and accept terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family safety / parental controls (Family Pairing)
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok announced a 'family safety mode' (screen time management option, restricted mode, and limit on direct messages) and expanded parental controls called 'Family Pairing' providing parents and guardians with educational resources about children's exposure; content for the feature was created with Internet Matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes available parental-control features and resources enabling guardians to manage young users' experiences on the platform; useful for parents and schools assessing children's app use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content moderation and censorship policies (global overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok's internal guidelines against the promotion of violence, separatism, and 'demonization of countries' have been criticized as non‑transparent; guidelines could be used to prohibit content related to topics such as the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests, Falun Gong, human rights in Tibet, Taiwan, and other politically sensitive subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarizes types of content that moderation policies target and the criticism of opacity. Important for journalists, activists, and creators working on political or human-rights topics to understand takedown risks and past controversies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Douyin (China) specific content restrictions and forbiddens
rubrics_metrics.description: Douyin guidelines forbid live broadcasting by unregistered foreigners, 'feudal superstition', 'money worship', smoking and drinking, competitive eating by the 'already obese', 'toxic' slime, 'pornographic' ASMR such as ear‑licking, and female anchors wearing revealing clothes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists region-specific prohibitions that differ from the international TikTok product; producers targeting Chinese-market Douyin must follow these stricter localized rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on sexual and LGBT/intersex content in moderation
rubrics_metrics.description: The consumption of alcohol, full or partial nudity, LGBT, and intersex contents were restricted even in places where they are legal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that certain categories of sexual/identity-related content have faced restrictions; creators should be cautious when posting such material, especially given regional variation in enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heating tool (manual promotion) policy and auditability
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'heating' tool allows TikTok to manually promote certain videos, comprising 1–2% of daily views; it was used to grow and diversify content and promote brands/artists/NGOs. Concerns arose about abuse (employees promoting their own accounts). TikTok said only a few individuals can approve heating in the US and promoted videos take up less than 0.002% of user feeds; future heating may be performed by vetted US security personnel and audited by third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes a non-algorithmic promotion mechanism and the safeguards and controversies around it; relevant for brands and creators seeking paid or platform-level amplification or assessing fairness/transparency of promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: STEM feed and third‑party reliability/safety partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok introduced a dedicated feed for STEM content that works with Common Sense Networks to check for safety and age appropriateness and with the Poynter Institute for reliability of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows platform attempts to curate specialized content with third‑party partners to improve safety and reliability; developers of educational content should be aware of such curation pipelines and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viral trends and harm risk (examples and platform response)
rubrics_metrics.description: The app has spawned numerous viral trends, some causing harm (e.g., 'devious licks' vandalism, the 'Kia Challenge' leading to crashes and deaths, cosmetic surgery trends, risky streaming stunts). TikTok has taken measures to remove and prevent access to some of these harmful trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents real-world harms arising from platform trends and the platform's reactive moderation; public-safety officials, educators, and creators should factor potential offline harms when sharing or amplifying challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency measures and external access to data/protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: After scrutiny, TikTok said it is granting some outside experts access to the platform's anonymized data sets and protocols, including filters, keywords, criteria for heating, and source code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates steps toward transparency and third‑party review; useful for researchers and policymakers evaluating claims about algorithmic bias, censorship, or foreign influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing, partnerships, and platform product experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: The article documents licensing deals (e.g., Sony, Warner), product experiments and services (TikTok Music, Live Studio, Notes, Local Feed, digital gift cards), and issues such as Live Studio's use of OBS code raising GPL compliance questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides examples of monetization, product expansion, and legal/compliance risks creators and partners should consider when using or integrating with the platform.
